entries.title: Jeremiah 33:1
segments: To the Old Testament church, the promise of a coming Saviour was the highest possible pledge that the gates of hell should never prevail against her.  She could not perish, because of her was to come the Redeemer of men.  The victory gained by Christ over the prince of this world, and his exaltation to the right hand of God, are, in like manner, a perfect pledge to the Christian church that God will make her triumphant over all opposition.  Sooner shall heaven and earth pass away than Christ, to whom the Father has given all power in heaven and earth, fail of subduing all things to himself.

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:2
segments: The maker thereof--that formed it; the words "thereof" and "it" seem to refer to God's gracious purpose concerning his covenant people that is revealed in the present chapter.

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:6
segments: I will bring it health and cure; God will not abate his present judgments upon Jerusalem, but he gives the gracious assurance of a future restoration.

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:15
segments: The Branch--unto David; the Messiah.  Compare

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:17
segments: David shall never want a man; literally, "there shall not be cut off to David a man;" that is, royal line shall not become extinct so that his kingdom can never be restored and perpetuated in his offspring.  For their chastisement, God prohibited David's children from the exercise of the kingly office through a long period of time,
; but the kingdom itself was reserved for Christ the son of David.

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:18
segments: Neither shall the priests the Levites want a man; after a temporary suspension, the Levitical priesthood was restored and continued till it was superseded by the perfect priesthood of Christ, which it typified.

entries.title: Jeremiah 33:24
segments:
This people; probably the Chaldeans, who were besieging the city. 
 
  The two families; Judah and Israel.
